classification.difficultyReason: The student measures a segment on a divided bar by subtracting its boundary positions. They express it as a fraction or percentage of the 10 cm bar, then apply that to the total. There is no numerical scale, so they must decide on the representation themselves. This is slightly more than a direct reading of a chart but is less than p35-q8, which has several parts and a labelled scale.

content.prompt: Each bar below is $10\text{ cm}$ long. Use a ruler to answer each part.

children.label: a
children.prompt: This bar represents the $800$ passengers on a ferry. Estimate how many passengers were students.

answer.worked:
The students' segment measures approximately $3\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Passengers per centimetre}&=800\div10=80\\\text{Students}&\approx3\times80=240\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: This bar represents the $1200$ trees in a plantation. Estimate how many trees were eucalypts.

answer.worked:
The eucalypt segment measures approximately $2.5\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}\text{Trees per centimetre}&=1200\div10=120\\\text{Eucalypts}&\approx2.5\times120=300\end{align*}$$
